ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Republic of Korea: Act on Reporting and Using Specified Financial Transaction Information, Act No. 6516 of November 28, 2001, as amended, including Articles 5-2, 5-3 and 5-4; Enforcement Decree of the Act on Reporting and Using Specified Financial Transaction Information, Presidential Decree No. 33711, as amended; Act on the Regulation of Concealment of Crime Proceeds, Act No. 6517 of November 28, 2001, as amended; Financial Services Commission regulations on customer due diligence, beneficial owner identification and verification, and reporting of suspicious transactions; Foreign Exchange Transactions Act, Act No. 17309 of May 26, 2020, as amended, Article 15 for foreign direct investment reporting. Beneficial ownership information is collected by financial institutions and disclosed to the Korea Financial Intelligence Unit and other competent government authorities only; there is no statutory public beneficial ownership register for ordinary Chusik Hoesa companies.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation (Korean equivalent: Certificate of Registered Corporate Matters from the District Court Registry)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Registry Office of the competent District Court, Supreme Court of Korea
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Parallel and mutually exclusive path: (A) for a destination state that is party to the Hague Apostille Convention, notarization where required, then issuance of a single Apostille certificate by the Korean Ministry of Foreign Affairs, and no consular legalization; (B) for a destination state that is not an Apostille Convention member, notarization where required, then certification by the Korean Ministry of Foreign Affairs, then consular legalization by the embassy or consulate of the destination country, and no Apostille certificate. Apostille and consular legalization are never chained together.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing (Korean equivalent: Corporate Registry Extract showing no dissolution, bankruptcy or liquidation notation, together with a tax compliance certificate)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Registry Office of the competent District Court, Supreme Court of Korea, and the National Tax Service district office with jurisdiction over the registered office
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Parallel and mutually exclusive path: (A) for a Hague Apostille Convention destination, certification by the Korean Ministry of Foreign Affairs through an Apostille after any required notarization, with no consular legalization; (B) for a non-member destination, certification by the Korean Ministry of Foreign Affairs followed by consular legalization at the destination embassy or consulate, with no Apostille. The selected path is determined solely by the destination country and the two paths are never applied sequentially.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution or Power of Attorney authorizing the incorporation process and foreign filings
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Company founders, board of directors, or shareholders, with notarization by a licensed Korean notary public
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Parallel and mutually exclusive path: (A) notarize the private corporate document before a Korean notary and then obtain an Apostille from the Korean Ministry of Foreign Affairs for use only in an Apostille Convention destination; (B) notarize the private corporate document before a Korean notary, authenticate it at the Korean Ministry of Foreign Affairs, and then obtain consular legalization from the destination embassy or consulate in Korea for use only in a non-member destination. Apostille and consular legalization are alternatives, never a sequential chain.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Articles of Association (Articles of Incorporation) of the Chusik Hoesa
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Company shareholders' meeting and Korean notary public, recorded in the corporate registry at the competent District Court
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Parallel and mutually exclusive path: (A) for Apostille Convention destinations, notarize the articles if required, then obtain a Korean Ministry of Foreign Affairs Apostille, and no consular legalization; (B) for non-Apostille destinations, notarize the articles if required, then obtain Korean Ministry of Foreign Affairs certification, then submit for consular legalization at the destination country's embassy or consulate in Korea, and no Apostille. The two legalization regimes are never combined.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank Reference Letter from a Korean commercial bank confirming the corporate relationship and account conduct
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Licensed commercial bank in South Korea holding or intending to hold the company corporate account
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Parallel and mutually exclusive path: (A) for a Hague Apostille Convention destination, have the bank's authorized signatory certify the letter, obtain notarization where required, and then obtain a Korean Ministry of Foreign Affairs Apostille; no consular legalization; (B) for a non-member destination, obtain notarization where required, then Korean Ministry of Foreign Affairs certification, then consular legalization by the destination embassy or consulate in Korea; no Apostille. Apostille and consular legalization are mutually exclusive routes and must never be chained.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: All UBOs, directors, officers, shareholders above 25 percent, and authorized signatories must be screened before onboarding and on an ongoing risk basis against the United Nations Security Council Consolidated List, the United States Office of Foreign Assets Control SDN and consolidated non-SDN lists, the European Union Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, the Republic of Korea sanctions list issued under the Act on Prohibition of Trading with Countries Subject to Economic Sanctions, and the Korean Financial Intelligence Unit terrorism and proliferation financing designations. Enhanced due diligence is mandatory for domestic and foreign politically exposed persons, including immediate family members and close associates, with source of wealth and source of funds inquiry, senior-management approval, and periodic transaction monitoring. Suspicious transaction reports must be filed with the Korea Financial Intelligence Unit in accordance with statutory deadlines and threshold reporting rules.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: I-SARANG Internet Registration Search and Filing System operated by the Supreme Court of Korea, in coordination with the competent District Court Registry Office for trade name reservation and corporate registration
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: A Chusik Hoesa must have a registered corporate name in Korean script (Hangul) containing a distinctive element, an optional business-purpose indicator, and the statutory legal-form suffix equivalent to 'Chusik Hoesa' or its permitted abbreviation. Foreign-language names are permitted only as secondary trade names and must be transcribed into Hangul using the Revised Romanization of Korean or the established Korean notational practice. The name must not be identical to an existing registered trade name in the same business category and must not contain misleading industry terms; the official registry record is maintained in Korean, while English transliteration is used only for cross-border documents.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the District Court Registry Officer rejects a name reservation, the applicant may file a written appeal with the head of the competent Registry Office within 14 days of receiving the written rejection, stating the legal and factual grounds and attaching a revised name search report. The registry must re-examine the application and issue a written decision. If the rejection is maintained, the applicant may bring an administrative suit in the competent Administrative Court within 90 days of the final rejection under the Administrative Litigation Act. In the alternative, the applicant may obtain prior ministerial approval for any sensitive token, correct the Hangul transliteration, and submit a fresh reservation application without waiting for the appeal decision.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office or commercial mailbox is not permissible as the sole registered office for a delivery-only ghost kitchen or virtual brand operator in South Korea. The National Tax Service requires a physical place of business for business registration and value-added tax purposes, and the local district office and municipal food-safety authorities require an actual licensed kitchen or food-preparation facility for the mandatory food service business license. Korean banks will reject a corporate account application if the registered address is only a virtual office, because the account opening procedure requires physical-presence verification and a permit-matched operating location. A virtual office may be used only as a supplementary mailing or administrative address, never as the principal place of business.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Checklist: (1) verify that the registered address is the actual operating kitchen and that the food service business license is issued for that exact location; (2) inspect the lease agreement, utility bills, fire and safety inspection certificates, and ownership or sublease authorization; (3) confirm that delivery-tablet terminals, point-of-sale devices, kitchen equipment and food storage are present and operational; (4) maintain VAT invoices, employment contracts, payroll records and sanitary inspection records at the physical site. Quantified risk for a delivery-only cloud kitchen filing VAT refunds and using the standard corporate registration structure is approximately 25 percent within the first six months and 55 percent within the first twenty-four months, rising to 80 percent or higher if the company relies on a virtual office without a licensed kitchen on the premises.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea (Act No. 1000, as amended), specifically Articles 288, 289, 291, 292, 295, 296, 298, 312, 313, 317, 318 and 330, together with the Enforcement Decree of the Commercial Act and the Non-Contentious Litigation Registration Rules
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registration Division of the District Court with territorial jurisdiction over the Company's registered office, administered under the authority of the Supreme Court of Korea
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Incorporation Registration Application for Establishment of a Stock Company (Chusik Hoesa) under Article 317(2) of the Commercial Act, together with all mandatory statutory annexes
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: None. The Republic of Korea imposes no statutory minimum stated capital and no permanent blocked-escrow requirement for a Chusik Hoesa. However, the entire subscription price of every issued share must be fully paid by deposit into a dedicated Korean bank subscription deposit account before the incorporation registration is filed, and the bank-issued Capital Deposit Certificate must be submitted to the registry. The official court filing fee is variable, calculated principally as registration tax of 0.4% of stated capital plus an education surtax of 20%; the amount stated in this dossier assumes stated capital of KRW 100,000,000 and a representative exchange rate.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLUTION NO. 1 OF THE FIRST BOARD OF DIRECTORS OF [●] CHUSIK HOESA. WHEREAS, the Company is being incorporated as a Chusik Hoesa under the Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea; and WHEREAS, the Articles of Incorporation of the Company have been duly executed and notarized on [date], and the incorporators have completed the subscription list and have fully paid the initial share capital into the designated subscription deposit account. NOW, THEREFORE, the first Board of Directors, having a quorum lawfully present and all proceedings recorded in the minutes, unanimously adopts the following resolutions: 1. Registered Office. RESOLVED, that the registered office of the Company shall be maintained at [●], [●] District, [●], Republic of Korea; that such address is adopted as the statutory seat for all official communications, court service of process, board meetings, shareholder meetings, and government filings; and that the Representative Director is authorized to register such office with the competent District Court Registry and to change it only upon a subsequent board resolution. 2. Confirmation of Capital Subscription and Payment. RESOLVED, that the subscription list is ratified; that the initial issued capital is [●] Korean Won, divided into [●] ordinary shares of par value [●] Korean Won each; that each subscriber's binding subscription is confirmed in the amounts set forth in the subscription list; and that the aggregate subscription price has been deposited into the subscription account at [●] Bank, as evidenced by the Capital Deposit Certificate dated [date]. 3. Banking Authorizations. RESOLVED, that the Company shall open operating, payroll and delivery-payout settlement accounts at [●] Bank and any other commercial bank selected by management; that the Representative Director and Chief Financial Officer are appointed as authorized signatories; that all payments above [●] Korean Won require dual signatures; and that delivery-platform payouts from UberEats and DoorDash shall be routed exclusively to designated Company settlement accounts. 4. Statutory Officer Appointments. RESOLVED, that [●] is appointed Representative Director and Chief Executive Officer; that [●] is appointed Chief Financial Officer; that [●] is appointed Statutory Auditor to the extent required by law; and that each officer accepts office and shall execute the statutory takeover and acceptance instruments. 5. License and Governance Authorizations. RESOLVED, that management is directed to complete the incorporation registration, obtain the corporate seal certificate, business registration certificate, and all tax and food-service licenses required for the ghost kitchen operations, to procure environmental, civil defense and occupational safety clearances, and to execute all leases, platform agreements, bank documents and ancillary instruments necessary to make the Company fully operational.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting, Approval and Notarization of the Articles of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary Public admitted under the Republic of Korea Notary Public Act, operating within the territorial jurisdiction of the District Court covering the Company's planned registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Corporate counsel first verifies the availability of the proposed Korean corporate name through the online court registry name search system, confirms that the name is not confusingly similar to any existing legal entity, and then prepares the Korean-language Articles of Incorporation. The Articles must state the corporate name, the precise multi-brand delivery-only cloud kitchen business purpose, the registered office address, the total authorized capital, the number and par value of shares, the initial issued shares, the directors and statutory auditor provisions, the method of convening general meetings, and the fiscal year. Each incorporator must review and execute the Articles, and the notary verifies the legal capacity and identity of all subscribers. After notarization, the Articles are the foundational instrument for all subsequent capital deposit and registration filings.
required_dossiers: Draft Articles of Incorporation in Korean
Passport or Alien Registration Card of each incorporator
Corporate seal specimen declaration
Power of attorney of the formation agent
Foreign Exchange Transactions Act report confirmation for non-resident subscribers
Consent or lease confirmation for the registered office address
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary requires textual or structural amendments, the Articles shall be revised and re-executed by all incorporators. If a foreign subscriber cannot satisfy identification requirements, an apostilled passport copy and a legalized domestic identification certificate shall be supplied within three business days, and the notarization shall be rescheduled.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Opening of Subscription Deposit Account and Full Payment of Paid-in Share Capital
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Corporate banking division of a licensed commercial bank in the Republic of Korea, supervised by the Financial Services Commission
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Following notarization, the promoters or the authorized representative shall open a dedicated subscription deposit account in the planned corporate name at a commercial bank. All subscribers must deposit the full issue price of their subscribed shares into this account, and the bank must issue an official Capital Deposit Certificate evidencing the account number, depositor, total received amount, and date of receipt. For non-resident subscribers, the remitted funds must be declared under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act and received through an authorized foreign exchange bank. No part of the subscription funds may be withdrawn before the completion of incorporation registration except as expressly permitted by the Commercial Act. The original Capital Deposit Certificate must be preserved for submission to the District Court Registry.
required_dossiers: Notarized Articles of Incorporation
Original subscription list signed by all subscribers
Passport or Alien Registration Card of each subscriber
Source-of-funds statement and AML/KYC declarations
Bank account application and signature card
Foreign exchange remittance receipt or declaration confirmation
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank raises anti-money laundering or source-of-funds concerns, the subscribers shall provide bank statements, contract evidence, or inheritance and gift declarations. If the foreign exchange remittance is delayed, the settlement date shall be requested to be extended and the subscription deposit account re-credited before the Capital Deposit Certificate is issued.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Incorporation Registration with the District Court Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registration Division of the District Court with territorial jurisdiction over the registered office; operational supervision by the Supreme Court of Korea Registry Office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Immediately after full payment of the subscription price and in all events within the statutory deadline under the Commercial Act, the representative director or authorized agent files the Incorporation Registration Application with the District Court Registry. The registry officer checks whether the Articles have been notarized, whether the Capital Deposit Certificate is in the Company's possession, whether the subscription list is complete, and whether the first directors and statutory auditor have validly accepted office. The registration tax and education surtax are paid at the registry or through the court's electronic payment system. Upon approval, the registry assigns a registration number, and the Company acquires juridical personality from that moment. The certified certificate of incorporation registration and the certified copy of the register shall then be collected for use by banks, tax authorities, and licensing agencies.
required_dossiers: Prescribed Incorporation Registration Application form
Original notarized Articles of Incorporation
Original Capital Deposit Certificate
Subscription list
Acceptance statements of the first directors and auditor
Minutes of organizational meeting or written resolutions
Power of attorney and agent identification
Payment receipts for registration tax and education surtax
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registrar issues a supplementary order or correction notice, the Company shall promptly file the requested documents and resubmit the application. If the application remains pending beyond fourteen business days, counsel shall contact the duties court, request an expedited review, or, if the defect is substantive, withdraw and re-file the application with corrected attachments.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Business Registration, Corporate Tax Setup and Four-Major Insurance Enrollments
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: District Tax Office of the National Tax Service having jurisdiction over the registered office; National Health Insurance Service and Korea Workers Compensation and Welfare Service for four-major insurance registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After receiving the certified certificate of incorporation registration, the Company must promptly file a corporate business registration application with the competent National Tax Service district office. This step produces the eleven-digit business registration number, corporate tax identification number, value-added tax identification number, and electronic tax invoice issuance certificate. The Company must register payroll and employees for national pension, national health insurance, employment insurance, and industrial accident compensation insurance through the Integrated Social Insurance Collection Portal, and must file mandatory withholding and value-added tax registration with the tax office. This registration is a precondition for opening fully functional corporate bank accounts and for executing delivery-platform payout agreements with UberEats and DoorDash.
required_dossiers: Certified certificate of incorporation registration
Certificate of corporate seal registration
Corporate business registration application form
Registered office lease agreement or ownership deed
Representative director identification documents
Corporate bank account certificate
Shareholder and foreign investor identification information
Four-major insurance registration forms and payroll data
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the National Tax Service requests correction of business purpose codes or representative director information, the Company shall file a revised application and attach the corporate seal certificate. If the tax ID issuance is delayed because a foreign director lacks a Korean tax identification number, the Company shall appoint a domestic tax representative, submit a power of attorney, and on the same day file a business registration correction.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Ghost Kitchen Food Service Business Permit, Environmental and Civil Defense Clearances
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministry of Food and Drug Safety delegated to the local Si/Gun/Gu district government Food Sanitation Department; National Fire Agency; Ministry of Environment; and Korea Occupational Safety and Health Agency
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The Company must submit an application for a Food Service Business Permit or, if the central kitchen model falls within the food manufacturing classification, a Food Manufacturing and Processing Business License, depending on the final facility protocol. The district health office shall inspect the commercial kitchen premises to confirm separate cooking and washing zones, sanitary hand-washing facilities, refrigerated storage, pest control measures, ventilation hoods, grease traps, delivery-packaging areas, and compliance with food handler health requirements. After the permit is issued, the Company must secure a Civil Defense fire-safety inspection certificate covering extinguishers, emergency exits, fire alarms, and gas safety. The facility must also file a wastewater discharge confirmation with the local municipal environment department and complete an occupational safety risk assessment for kitchen equipment and employees.
required_dossiers: Food Service Business Permit application form
Business registration certificate
Registered office or kitchen lease and floor plan
Licensed wastewater and sewage connection certificate
Fire-safety compliance application and building use certificate
Food handler health certificates
Menu formulation and delivery-zone statement
Hazard analysis and critical control points plan if required
Civil defense inspection checklist and gas safety certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the district health office issues a request for supplementation or an improvement order, the Company shall cure the noted deficiency within fourteen days and request reinspection. If the permit is denied on grounds of structural nonconformity, the Company shall modify the kitchen layout, submit revised architectural drawings, and appeal the administrative decision through the provincial governor or Administrative Litigation Act procedures.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministry of Food and Drug Safety (MFDS) and the local Si/Gun/Gu district government, jointly with the Ministry of Environment, the National Fire Agency, and the Korea Occupational Safety and Health Agency
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Food Service Business Permit under the Food Sanitation Act, supplemented by a Food Manufacturing and Processing Business License if the facility produces packaged or semi-processed food for multiple virtual brands

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry of Environment of the Republic of Korea, Korean Environmental Corporation, and local municipal water and sewer department
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category C (Low-Impact Small-Scale Facility). A full Environmental Impact Assessment is not required for an ordinary urban delivery-only ghost kitchen with a gross floor area below the EIA Act thresholds; only a simplified municipal wastewater discharge notification, grease-trap registration, and odor compliance registration are mandatory. If the facility increases in scale beyond the EIA thresholds or installs own wastewater treatment equipment, a detailed environmental review will be triggered.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater discharged to the public sewer shall meet the local ordinance limits applicable to food-service facilities, generally BOD no greater than 300 mg/L, COD no greater than 300 mg/L,

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) of the Republic of Korea; online electronic portal: HomeTax (www.hometax.go.kr). Customs export filings are separately processed through Korea Customs Service UNI-PASS.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a domestic Chusik Hoesa, the company's representative or appointed tax agent must apply for a Business Registration Number from the district tax office of the NTS with jurisdiction over the registered head office before commencing business, and no later than 20 days after commencement. The application is filed electronically through HomeTax's 'Business Registration' service using the certificate of incorporation under the Commercial Act, the corporate registration certificate, the head-office lease or ownership evidence, and representative identification. A foreign non-resident entity that has no domestic office but makes taxable supplies in Korea, including electronic services, must appoint a tax representative and obtain a Business Registration Number by filing a non-resident business registration application through HomeTax; the non-resident VAT returns must be filed through that tax representative. The Business Registration Number serves as both the corporate TIN and the VAT registration identifier.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None. The Chusik Hoesa is classified by statute as a corporation under the Commercial Act and is a separate income tax and VAT taxpayer. Korean tax law does not provide a check-the-box or other voluntary entity-classification election. Anti-hybrid mismatch rules apply automatically and cannot be varied by taxpayer election.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value-Added Tax (VAT) under the Value-Added Tax Act (Republic of Korea)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: None. VAT registration is mandatory from the first taxable supply in Korea; there is no statutory turnover threshold before registration is required. A simplified taxable person regime exists for eligible individual businesses with annual turnover of KRW 80 million or less, but it does not waive registration and is not available to a Chusik Hoesa corporate taxpayer.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory electronic tax invoicing through HomeTax. VAT-registered businesses must issue an Electronic Tax Invoice for every B2B supply and transmit the invoice data to the NTS within one day after issuance; approved e-invoice service providers integrate through NTS APIs. There is no additional physical fiscal stamp or continuous real-time transaction clearance, but the NTS performs digital cross-checking and pre-issue validation. For B2C restaurant delivery sales, card settlement data is transmitted to the NTS through approved card acquirers, and cash receipts must be issued through the HomeTax cash receipt system.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: A supply of goods qualifies for 0% VAT when the goods are actually exported from Korea under an Export Declaration accepted by Korea Customs Service, title and risk pass to a foreign buyer, and export proceeds are collected in foreign currency or through an NTS- and Foreign Exchange Transactions Act-approved settlement method. Qualifying offshore digital services and other services are zero-rated only when supplied to a non-resident customer, the service is actually used outside Korea, and the consideration is paid in foreign currency or through an approved Korean foreign-exchange settlement account. Domestic food delivery sales in Korea, including orders fulfilled through international platform payment rails, are deemed domestic consumption and remain taxable at 10%.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Electronic Export Declaration and export declaration receipt issued by Korea Customs Service through UNI-PASS
Bill of Lading (sea) or Air Waybill (air)
Foreign exchange bank certificate or foreign-currency receipt confirmation issued by a licensed Korean foreign exchange bank evidencing receipt of export proceeds
Sales contract or service agreement evidencing the foreign counterparty and place of consumption
Documentary evidence of offshore service use or digital-content access outside Korea, where zero-rating is claimed for offshore services
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The NTS and Korea Customs Service will verify export declarations against customs clearance records, shipping documents, bank receipts, and foreign-exchange settlement records. If zero-rating is applied fraudulently or without complete substantiation, the refunded VAT is clawed back with additional tax and interest under the Value-Added Tax Act and Framework Act on National Taxes; false or fraudulent tax invoices and fake export schemes are subject to enhanced penalty taxes, criminal referral under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act, and personal liability of directors. Exporters must retain all supporting documentation for at least five years from the relevant filing deadline and must settle export proceeds within 180 days; failure to repatriate within the statutory deadline may cause the export zero-rating to be revoked.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Korea (BOK) and the Ministry of Economy and Finance (MOEF) under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act and subordinate Foreign Exchange Transactions Regulations
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: South Korea operates a free-float and de jure convertible currency regime for current account transactions, but maintains a regulated capital account framework. The KRW is freely convertible for trade-related payments, service transactions, dividends, and profit remittances, provided the underlying activity is documented and filed with the designated foreign exchange bank. Non-resident equity injections into a Chusik Hoesa are treated as foreign direct investment and require a reporting notice via the Korea Trade-Investment Promotion Agency (KOTRA) or a delegated foreign exchange bank, after which the capital may be brought in as foreign exchange or KRW. Capital account items such as foreign currency loans, overseas deposits, and portfolio flows are still subject to a registration and reporting regime, and the Bank of Korea can impose temporary stabilization measures during extraordinary market volatility. Profit remittance to overseas shareholders necessitates a tax clearance certificate, audited financial statements, and evidence of the board resolution declaring dividends. There are no mandatory surrender requirements today, as the prior surrender system was abolished; exporters may retain foreign currency earnings in designated foreign exchange accounts. However, all receipts must be properly credited under the correct transaction purpose code and supported by underlying trade or service contracts to avoid anti-money laundering scrutiny. The practical concreteness of this convertibility implies that a treasury operation should pre-clear large transfers with the relationship bank and maintain complete primary documentation for every inward and outward flow.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Export proceeds from the ghost kitchen's online sales or third-party marketplace payouts must be received by the Korean entity within five years from the export declaration acceptance date as per Article 9 of the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act. There is no mandatory conversion ratio into KRW; the foreign currency can be held in an authorized foreign exchange account at a domestic bank. The proceeds must be collected via an authorized foreign exchange bank or a permitted payment settlement institution, and the underlying export declaration must be filed with the Korea Customs Service.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account (Foreign Currency Deposit) and Basic Operational Chusik Hoesa Checking Account
Capital Escrow Account and Basic Operational KRW Account with Cross-Border Settlement
Capital Escrow Account and Basic Operational Currency Account
Capital Escrow Account and Basic Operational Account with Trade Finance Integration

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Offshore fintech EMI providers and virtual account platforms carry Low feasibility for a Korean Chusik Hoesa. Under the Electronic Financial Transactions Act, any institution receiving, transmitting, or settling payment instructions in Korea must be licensed by the Financial Services Commission or operate as a registered electronic financial business. Most neobanking app providers from outside Korea do not hold a domestic e-money license and therefore cannot legally provide a primary account or issuance of KRW-denominated transaction accounts. They may help the entity connect to domestic payment gateways such as Inicis, KG Inicis, or Toss Payments, but these act as merchants' acquiring processors rather than full banking counterparts. The corporate treasury should rely exclusively on a domestic Tier-1 commercial bank for the core capital and disbursement accounts, and can use an overseas EMI only for non-Korean side accumulation if such EMI is licensed in the counterparty jurisdiction.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: The statutory directors, particularly the final beneficial owner and the named representative director, are generally required to appear in-branch for an in-person identity verification and anti-money laundering interview during the initial onboarding process. Remote consular proxy opening is not accepted as a default path by Korean banks because the Act on Reporting and Use of Specific Financial Transaction Information imposes a mandatory face-to-face customer due diligence step for corporate entities. A remote video call may be used only as a supplemental validation after the in-person visit. If a foreign director cannot travel to Korea, the bank may accept a notarized and apostilled power of attorney granted to a local representative, but that representative must still appear physically, and the foreign director's identity must be independently verified through a certified passport copy and a 6-month recent bank statement utility bill as proof of residential address.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Mismatch between the declared business purpose of a holding company and actual high-volume delivery aggregator settlements from multiple overseas platforms (UberEats and DoorDash) without corresponding local-currency revenue records.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: CEO or compliance officer signed business model narrative, the ISIC 5610 ghost kitchen license, signed commercial agreements with each delivery aggregator, 3 months of platform revenue statements, and the Korea Customs Service import declarations for restaurant equipment or food ingredients if applicable.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unusual concentration of inbound transfer from a single overseas parent account to a newly opened corporate account immediately after incorporation, raising suspicion of layering or shell company structuring.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: The KOTRA foreign direct investment filing receipt, an audited or notarized reserve increase minutes, the board resolution approving share subscription, the Singapore or Hong Kong parent's banking reference letter, and a detailed capital contribution schedule showing the source of funds composed of electronically traceable share transfer operations.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inconsistencies between the registered address shown on the corporate certificate and the physical location where food preparation, storage, or delivery dispatch occurs, especially if the entity offers virtual brands without a physical storefront.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A valid commercial lease agreement for the ghost kitchen facility, a photograph of the facility entrance and signage, a utility bill for the facility under the company name, and the local municipal food service license or business registration certificate reflecting the actual kitchen address.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Frequent and irregular withdrawals in small-denomination KRW cash amounts from the corporate account after settlement payments from delivery platforms, which can indicate a tip-jar or under-the-table salary structure inconsistent with the declared payroll.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Complete payroll register with employment contracts for every kitchen worker, social insurance premium statements, labor union notification if any, quarterly withholding tax returns, and contemporaneous approved expense reports for cash purchases of perishable groceries and wages.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: The initial shareholder capital or later equity injections from the non-resident parent must follow the Foreign Direct Investment (FDI) reporting route. The Chusik Hoesa's foreign investor files a pre-funding FDI notification with KOTRA or a delegated domestic bank, and the bank then issues a Certificate of Foreign Direct Investment Registration. After the notification, the inbound wire travels via SWIFT MT103 through a designated foreign exchange bank; the purpose code should identify equity investment in a domestic corporation. The bank will perform a source-of-funds review and verify the investor's identity, board approval, and the issuance of new shares in the company register. Following receipt, the bank issues a certificate of inward remittance for capital verification and the company must file the subsequent post-investment report to KOTRA within 30 days, including the investment amount and share details. All documents must be kept in the corporate treasury file for a minimum of five years.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: The principal clearing rail for outbound operational disbursements in the ghost kitchen structure is the SWIFT MT103 wire for cross-border payments such as procurement of imported ingredients, software subscriptions, insurance, digital licensing fees, and royalties. For larger equipment acquisitions or packaging supplies, a commercial letter of credit (LC) is advisable, as Korean banks will prioritize an LC when the beneficiary is a Chinese or Southeast Asian supplier requiring payment security upon presentation of transport documents. Documentary collections such as D/P and D/A may be used for low-complexity, repeated disbursements to trusted counterparties; all trade-associated documents must be retained due to Korea's trade declaration obligations. For domestic disbursements and payroll of Korean kitchen staff, the entity will use the KRW current account with local interbank clearing via the Hong Kong Interbank Clearing system analogous, only for Korean institutions through the Bank of Korea's Payment and Settlement System. The treasury should align each outward transfer with the underlying commercial contract and confirm the applicable foreign exchange purpose code on every instruction.
fx_hedging_instruments: Chusik Hoesa is permitted to use covered transactional forward contracts with a licensed foreign exchange bank to hedge the KRW/USD exposure arising from committed payables or receivables; the forward must have documentary proof of a valid underlying trade transaction.

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) are only permitted to Korean banking entities and non-resident investors under limited circumstances; a Chusik Hoesa engaged in real operational revenue may execute an NDF only when a physical deliverable forward is impractical and the bank confirms exemption under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act.

Currency swaps are not generally available to a wholly domestic Korean operational legal entity without a specific large-scale cross-border cash flow; only authorized financial institutions may enter into cross-currency swaps, so the treasury should rely on layered natural hedging through multi-currency accounts and timely FX conversion rather than speculative instruments.

Plain vanilla currency options with designated banks are permissible for hedging a known future cash flow, but the bank will require monthly board-approved treasury policies and underlying trade documents to prevent speculative intent.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate income tax return and self-assessment (corporation tax settlement)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) via the district tax office with jurisdiction over the registered office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 3 months after the end of the fiscal year; if the fiscal year ends on 31 December, the filing and payment deadline is 31 March of the following year. The filing deadline may be extended by a maximum of one month with the NTS approval, and up to five months where the company maintains books abroad.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file or understatement of tax base triggers a non-filing penalty of 20% of the tax payable (or 10% for understatement, capped at KRW 100 million), plus overdue interest of approximately 0.022% per day (8.03% per annum) until paid. Repeated non-compliance allows the NTS to demand additional supporting documents, impose enhanced penalties, collect tax through asset seizure, and expose directors to civil liability; persistent non-filing may be grounds for a court petition for dissolution, though there is no automatic administrative strike-off for tax delinquency.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Local income tax (residence tax) on corporation tax
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Local government (municipal tax office of the si/gun/gu where the registered office is located)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Identical to the corporation tax deadline: within 3 months of fiscal year-end (31 March for calendar-year taxpayers). The local tax is 10% of the corporate income tax paid.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: An under-filing surcharge of 10% of the unpaid local income tax plus a late payment surcharge of 3% immediately, and then 0.022% per day; municipal authorities may pursue forced collection through property attachment. There is no related strike-off trigger, but director liability and eventual judicial dissolution remain possible for extreme non-compliance.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Ordinary general meeting of shareholders and board approval of annual financial statements
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Shareholders' meeting (internal governance action; no filing with a government authority, but the approved statements and minutes must be retained in the company's statutory books)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: The ordinary general meeting must be convened within 3 months after the end of each fiscal year (for a 31 December fiscal year, no later than 31 March).
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: If the meeting is not convened in time, any shareholder may petition a court for a summons. Directors may be subject to an administrative fine of up to KRW 5 million for failing to prepare or submit financial statements; knowingly issuing false statements triggers criminal penalties. Non-compliance alone does not result in an automatic strike-off, but the court may order dissolution upon a request from interested parties if the company fails to comply with mandatory corporate governance obligations.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Statutory balance-sheet publication (announcement of financial statements)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: No receiving government authority; publication must be made either in the Official Gazette or in a daily newspaper or via the company's electronic announcement channel
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 2 weeks after the ordinary general shareholders' meeting (for calendar-year companies, ordinarily by 14 April).
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to publish subjects the relevant directors to an administrative fine of up to KRW 5 million and exposes the company to creditor claims for access to financial statements. In case of fraudulent publication, criminal sanctions under the Commercial Act may apply. No automatic strike-off; however, persistent violations can be leveraged in a court dissolution action.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Independent external audit report (if the company is a statutory audit target) and filing of audited financial statements
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Financial Supervisory Service (FSS) and the shareholders' meeting; the audit report is also presented to the Korean Institute of Certified Public Accountants (KICPA) as necessary
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: The audit report must be delivered to the company in time for the ordinary shareholders' meeting (i.e., before the AGM). If the company is subject to external audit, the company must submit the audit report and audited financial statements to the FSS within 5 days after the ordinary shareholders' meeting. For calendar-year companies this normally means filing by 5 April.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to appoint an outside auditor or failure to submit the audit report to the FSS may result in an administrative order and penalties up to KRW 20 million; auditors who issue false opinions face criminal punishment and revocation of CPA license. The absence of a required audit report will cause the tax authorities to disallow deductions and increase assessment risk. The company is still not automatically struck off, but may be judicially dissolved if compliance failure is persistent and egregious.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual foreign investment management report (for a foreign-invested company with foreign equity ratio of 10% or more)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy (MOTIE) through KOTRA Foreign Investment Support Center
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 90 days after the end of the fiscal year (by 31 March for a calendar-year fiscal year).
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to submit the annual report can trigger an administrative fine of up to KRW 2 million under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act, and it may jeopardise foreign investment incentives or tax benefits. If the company fails to maintain the foreign investment status, it may lose recognition as a foreign-invested company, though there is no direct strike-off consequence.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Under the Act on External Audit of Stock Companies, an independent statutory audit by a licensed certified public accountant is mandatory for any stock company (Chusik Hoesa) that meets any of the following criteria at the end of the fiscal year: (a) total assets exceed KRW 12 billion (approximately USD 8.9 million, at 1,350 KRW/USD); (b) the company is a listed issuer or an entity whose securities are publicly offered; (c) the company is a financial institution, insurance company, securities company, or other entity designated by the Financial Services Commission; (d) the company is a holding company subject to the Monopoly Regulation and Fair Trade Act; or (e) the company is designated as an audit target by the Financial Services Commission based on debt, revenue, or public-interest criteria. In addition, even if total assets are below KRW 12 billion, any shareholder holding at least 1% of outstanding shares may demand an external audit under the same Act. A mandatory audit report must include an opinion on the financial statements prepared on a going-concern basis.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Korean International Financial Reporting Standards (K-IFRS) are the governing accounting standards. Companies subject to a statutory external audit are required to apply K-IFRS (if they are listed or large companies) or the Korean Generally Accepted Accounting Principles (K-GAAP) as adopted for Small and Medium-Sized Entities (SME Accounting Standards) where the company qualifies as an SME and is not otherwise required to use K-IFRS. For all statutory audit targets, financial statements shall give a true and fair view and comply with the Accounting Standards and the Audit Standards set by the Korean Institute of Certified Public Accountants.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Korean commercial law does not provide for a standalone annual UBO (ultimately beneficial owner) confirmation form for a private Chusik Hoesa. Instead, the company is required to maintain an up-to-date Register of Members that records every issuance and transfer of shares, the date of transfer, the parties, the number of shares, and the transferor's and transferee's names, addresses, and resident registration or business registration numbers. Any transfer of shares must be reflected in the Register of Members upon the transferee's application and must be endorsed on the certificate. Under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act, a foreign-invested entity (foreign ownership at least 10%) must file an annual foreign investment management report within 90 days of fiscal year-end, and any change in foreign ownership, including every 10% or greater transfer, must be reported to MOTIE or the designated exchange bank within two weeks of the closing. There is no statutory 30-day reconformation window in South Korea; the analogous timeline is the 14-day period for registering structural changes (e.g., changes of directors, representatives, registered office, and capital) with the Commercial Registry, and the 30-day deadline for statutory internal books and records updates where the transaction affects the shareholder register if the transfer takes place after the books close.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 500 - USD 2,000 per annum for a registered office/agent service in Seoul or major municipal jurisdictions
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 5,000 - USD 20,000 per annum for a ghost kitchen / virtual brand operating company with statutory audit exposure

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 24% top marginal corporate income tax rate (progressive: 9% on tax base up to KRW 200 million; 19% from KRW 200 million to KRW 20 billion; 24% above KRW 20 billion)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Foreign-invested enterprises in Free Economic Zones may obtain a 5-year 100% corporate tax exemption followed by a 50% reduction for the next 2 years; domestic venture and SME regimes may provide income tax exemptions for qualifying new-growth businesses; R&D expenditures are eligible for super-deductions and tax credits; a patent box / intellectual property income regime can apply reduced effective rates to qualifying intangibles-derived income; no reliance is placed on informal or unwritten incentives.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Corporate Income Tax Return for Tax Base and Tax Amount (법인세 과세표준 및 세액 신고서), filed through the National Tax Service Hometax e-Filing Portal; official return equals the national corporate tax return prepared under Corporate Tax Act Article 60 and the Enforcement Decree.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual, with a mandatory interim prepayment return for fiscal years exceeding six months; interim prepayment is due within two months after the first half of the fiscal year.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The annual return must be filed within three months after the fiscal year-end; for a calendar-year corporation, the statutory deadline is March 31 of the following year, unless a valid extension is granted under the Framework Act on National Taxes and the Corporate Tax Act.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 1 - Entity Identification and Fiscal Period
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Enter the legal name of the Chusik Hoesa, business registration number, representative director, corporate tax classification, industry code (ISIC 5610 / NAICS 722513), fiscal year opening and closing dates, and the date of incorporation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Disclose the direct and indirect shareholding percentages of every non-resident shareholder; identify the tax treaty residence of each foreign investor; attach the relevant schedule showing treaty entitlement so that withholding at Box 7 can be reduced only where the non-resident beneficial owner supplies a valid Tax Residency Certificate.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report total revenue, cost of goods sold, gross profit, selling and general administrative expenses, operating income, non-operating income and expenses, and pre-tax book income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For the ghost-kitchen virtual-brand business, recognize the full gross delivery-platform payouts from UberEats and DoorDash as revenue; separately disclose platform commissions and delivery driver costs as deductible operating expenses; intercompany franchise fees or brand royalties paid to a foreign parent must be supported by written agreements and transfer pricing benchmarks before deduction.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 3 - Tax Reconciliation Adjustments to Taxable Income
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Reconcile book income to Korean taxable income by adding back non-deductible expenses (e.g., entertainment above statutory limits, donations above thresholds, deemed expenses) and subtracting tax-deductible items not recognized in the books (e.g., certain tax credits and loss carryforwards).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For cross-border transactions, add back excessive management fees, unreported deemed royalties, and non-arm's length intercompany charges; ensure foreign-related party adjustments follow the ordinary income calculation rules under Article 66 of the Corporate Tax Act and the Law for the Coordination of International Tax Affairs.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 4 - Tax Base Calculation and Loss Carryforward
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Compute the taxable income base by applying available loss carryforwards, non-taxable income, and deductions; verify the taxable base is not a negative amount.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Net operating loss carryforwards may be applied within the statutory 10-year limit; a foreign-owned entity may not use losses of a foreign head-office or sister entity; the Korean permanent establishment must compute its own taxable income based on Korean-source operating activities and the fiction of force-of-attraction under the domestic law.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 5 - Progressive Tax Rate and National Corporate Tax Payable
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Apply the statutory progressive corporate tax rates of 9%, 19%, and 24% to the taxable base to derive national corporate income tax; compute the local income tax surcharge, generally 10% of the national corporate income tax, and add it to the total corporate tax burden.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For non-resident corporations with a Korean permanent establishment, the taxable base attributable to the Korean PE is taxed at the same progressive rates; there is no separate branch tax treatment in the domestic law beyond the ordinary corporate income tax plus local surcharge, but remittances of PE profits must still be checked for branch-tax and treaty articles.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 6 - Foreign Tax Credits and Domestic Tax Credits
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Enter all creditable foreign taxes, tax credit limitations, R&D tax credits, investment tax credits, employment creation credits, and other statutory corporate tax credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign tax credits may offset Korean corporate income tax on foreign-source income only under the treaty/domestic credit limit; the credit must be supported by tax payment receipts and translated tax assessment documents; no credit is allowable for foreign taxes borne by another group company absent a valid Korean tax nexus.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 7 - Non-Resident Shareholder Dividend Withholding Schedules
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: List dividend distributions resolved and paid to non-resident shareholders, including cash and in-kind distributions, disproportionate distributions, and constructive dividends from non-arm's length transactions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If the foreign shareholder is not entitled to treaty relief, withhold 22% (20% national corporate/income tax plus 2% local surcharge) on dividends; if treaty relief is claimed, attach the Tax Residency Certificate, beneficial ownership declaration, and the application for reduction/exemption of non-resident tax; ensure the 10% or 15% treaty rate is applied only after the NTS accepts the reduced withholding and only to the extent the shareholder has substantive economic ownership and is not a conduit.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 8 - Controlled Transactions and Transfer Pricing Schedule
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Provide a detailed schedule of controlled transactions with foreign related parties: nature, amount, contractual terms, currencies, profit margins, and overall intercompany transfer pricing results.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Select the most appropriate arm's length method (CUP, Resale Price, Cost Plus, TNMM, or Profit Split); prepare Local File and Master File if the statutory thresholds are met; include an economic substance narrative showing Korean-based delivery operations, kitchen management, brand supervision, and personnel decision-making as Core Income-Generating Activities in Korea.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late non-filing or under-filing attracts a 20% negligence penalty, while fraudulent or unfair misstatement attracts a 40% penalty under Article 47-2 and Article 47-3 of the Framework Act on National Taxes; unfaithfully filed returns incur a 10% underreporting penalty; unpaid tax attracts daily interest and surcharges roughly equivalent to annual statutory late-payment interest rates; repeated or serious evasion may trigger criminal prosecution under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act with imprisonment up to three years or a fine up to three times the evaded tax; foreign shareholders or directors subject to undisclosed outbound distributions may face blacklisting and overseas departure restrictions by the National Tax Service.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 22% statutory combined withholding on outbound dividends to non-residents (20% national withholding tax plus 2% local income tax surcharge); no withholding is required on distributions to another Korean domestic corporation but the full 22% applies to non-resident shareholders absent a treaty.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To claim Double Tax Treaty relief, the non-resident beneficial owner must (i) submit a valid Tax Residency Certificate issued by the treaty country's competent authority, (ii) complete an Application for Exemption or Reduction of Non-Resident Tax before the withholding agent or competent Korean district tax office, (iii) provide a beneficial ownership statement proving it is not a conduit, and (iv) substantiate that it meets treaty limitations-on-benefits clauses and the OECD principal purpose test; the withholding agent must retain all documentation, and if the Korean NTS has not granted approval by the payment date, the statutory 22% must be withheld pending a refund mechanism for the treaty rate differential.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory withholding on cross-border royalties and interest is 22% (20% national plus 2% local surcharge); under most Korean Comprehensive Double Tax Agreements the treaty rate for interest and royalties is reduced to 10%, with some treaties providing 15%, subject to submission of the Tax Residency Certificate, beneficial ownership evidence, and satisfaction of the treaty's limitation-on-benefits provisions before the payment date.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: KRW 10 billion in aggregate cross-border related-party transactions triggers mandatory Local File / Master File preparation; additional group-revenue thresholds apply for the Custody-by-Country Report and integrated tax report under the Law for the Coordination of International Tax Affairs and its Enforcement Decree.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Korea does not apply an UAE-style Economic Substance Regulations code, but the National Tax Service applies a rigorous economic substance and substance-over-form doctrine; a Chusik Hoesa must demonstrate Core Income-Generating Activities in Korea, including actual kitchen staff, delivery-platform contracting, inventory management, order processing, accounting records, and senior management decisions; if the entity before being a bare invoicing shell or conduit, the NTS may re-characterize the arrangement, deny treaty benefits, impose transfer pricing adjustments, and attribute the income to the real foreign principal under Korean tax law.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion / Fraudulent Understatement of Ghost-Kitchen Revenue
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberately omitting or understating gross delivery-platform revenues received from UberEats, DoorDash, and virtual-brand apps; creating fake cost invoices; inflating food-wastage deductions; or shifting revenue to shell affiliates without arm's length remuneration.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: 40% unfair tax penalty under Article 47-3 of the Framework Act on National Taxes, plus daily late-payment interest; criminal liability under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act (imprisonment up to three years or a fine up to three times the evaded tax amount).
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are jointly and severally liable for unpaid corporate tax where corporate assets are insufficient and the insufficiency results from intentional or grossly negligent director conduct; assets may be seized and directors may be placed on a tax-delinquent blacklist with a travel ban preventing overseas departure; a criminal conviction can result in imprisonment, restitution orders, and disqualification from serving as directors.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: International Withholding Tax and DTA Benefit Abuse
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Paying dividends, royalties, or interest to a non-resident parent or affiliate without withholding the statutory tax, applying a treaty-reduced rate without a valid Tax Residency Certificate or beneficial ownership proof, or structuring payments through a conduit jurisdiction lacking economic substance solely to obtain lower DTA withholding rates.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The withholding agent is jointly liable for the un-withheld tax under the Framework Act on National Taxes and the Corporate Tax Act, plus a 10% penalty for unfaithful reporting and 40% for fraudulent non-withholding; interest accrues from the original payment date; the NTS may disallow the deduction for the underlying royalty/interest payment.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Representative directors who knowingly fail to withhold are personally liable for the full withheld amount, penalties and interest; the director may be blacklisted with a departure restriction for delinquent taxes exceeding statutory thresholds; intentional evasion triggers criminal referral, with imprisonment up to three years and civil asset restitution for dividends improperly distributed.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Corporation and Transfer Pricing Non-Compliance with No Real Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating the Korean Chusik Hoesa as a paper entity with no employees, no kitchen lease, no delivery-platform contracts, no Korean board authority, or no intercompany pricing documentation; related-party transactions with the foreign virtual-brand parent are not supported by contracts and are performed at non-arm's length prices; the Korean entity lacks the Core Income-Generating Activities.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The NTS may re-characterize the arrangement under economic substance doctrine, adjust taxable income to the arm's length result, impose a 40% fraudulent understatement penalty, and deny treaty benefits; failure to prepare and submit transfer pricing documentation may trigger separate documentation penalties under the Law for the Coordination of International Tax Affairs.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Courts may pierce the corporate veil when the entity is a pure alter ego, holding directors personally liable for corporate taxes and civil restitution; directors face departure restrictions through administrative blacklisting, personal liability for foreign withholding tax shortfalls, and criminal imprisonment where fraudulent documentation or false tax returns are used to conceal the sham.
